title: The Reality of Other People’s Money
hook_text: DEALS ARE NEVER BUILT ON SAVINGS

beats.say: Deals are never built on savings.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of a heavy steel vault door half-open in a dark, dimly lit concrete room.

beats.say: Big moves require using other people's money to scale fast.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person in a sharp coat walking past a towering glass skyscraper at dusk.

beats.say: Entrepreneurs lean on lenders, investors, and partners to fund major acquisitions.
beats.visual: Close-up of a sleek brass fountain pen resting on a heavy oak desk next to a blank paper.

beats.say: It’s how businesses grow from local shops into massive enterprises.
beats.visual: An aerial drone shot of busy city traffic moving through a concrete interchange at twilight.

beats.say: But here's the catch nobody mentions in the pitch decks.
beats.visual: A dim vintage desk lamp casting long shadows over a stack of unread financial documents.

beats.say: You either owe that money right back with interest.
beats.visual: A close-up of a mechanical calculator printing a long tape of numbers on white paper.

beats.say: Or you hand over a massive chunk of your company's equity.
beats.visual: A hand sliding a blank white puzzle piece away from a completed puzzle on a table.

beats.say: Outside capital always wants a return, and it demands control.
beats.visual: A person standing with their back to the camera, looking out a large rainy office window.
A close-up of heavy brass scales tipping unevenly under a small weight.

beats.say: It also magnifies every single mistake you make along the way.
beats.visual: A stack of dark wooden blocks wobbling precariously on a polished dark wood table.

beats.say: Understand the true cost of funding because you're always paying for
beats.visual: A dark cinematic view of a quiet urban street lit by a single orange amber streetlight.

caption:
Other people's money builds empires, but it always demands a price. Know the trade-offs before you sign. 

#moneypsychology #personalfinance #wealthbuilding #businesstips #financialeducation
description: An honest look at how major deals are funded using other people's money, and the hidden cost of taking on debt or giving up equity.
first_comment: Would you rather give up equity or take on debt to grow?

facts.claim: OPM and OPR involve using lenders, investors, and partners to fund deals.
facts.basis: Dan Peña framework on OPM and OPR.

facts.claim: The catch of OPM is debt repayment or loss of equity ownership.
facts.basis: The honest catch regarding outside capital.
